title: polyEval at degree bound 0 is zero (the empty sum)
statement: CReal.polyEval c 0 x is Equiv-equal (in fact Eq) to CReal.zero for any coefficient function c and point x -- the base equation of polyEval's own recursive unfolding.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.polyEval_zero : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> CReal)) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> Eq.{1} CReal (CReal.polyEval x0 AxNat.zero x1) CReal.zero))

evidence.supports: CReal.polyEval_zero is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example theorem_dependency_inventory -- CReal.polyEval_zero 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^CReal\.polyEval_zero[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: The producing prelude admits CReal.polyEval_zero through the trusted Kernel::add_declaration gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type. theorem_dependency_inventory exits non-zero for a named filter matching nothing (a deleted/renamed theorem cannot read as a re-derived one), and grep -c (never -q) both avoids a SIGPIPE-under-pipefail false negative and independently asserts the exact tab-anchored line is present. --release is MANDATORY: this tool also builds creal/complex/cpoint, which overflow the default debug thread stack.
